$QQQ gamma map is set up for downside and it's not even close

Quick explainer for anyone who hasn't seen one of these. This is a GEX heatmap. It basically shows where dealers are stuck hedging at each strike.

Green/yellow = positive gamma. Dealers buy dips, sell rips there. Price gets pinned, moves slow down.
Dark/purple = negative gamma. Dealers have to sell as price falls. No cushion. Moves get fast and ugly.

Now look at the actual numbers on this map

Below price: -$3.9B
Above price: +$1.8B

That's the whole story. More than 2x the pressure below us than above us.

Above, 685-690 is stacked green. That's why every single bounce this week got sold right there. It's a wall.

Below is where it gets interesting. The nodes just keep getting darker the lower you go. 682, 667, 659, 655... and then there's the 650 strike for Nov 20 expiry sitting at like -$1.6B. That one node is massive.

If 660 goes and 647 (November low) breaks, dealers hedging that book aren't catching the knife, they're selling into it. 650 becomes a magnet. And 650 is basically the doorway to the 620-630 January shelf I've been talking about all week.

Honest part though, because I don't want anyone treating this like gospel

This map redraws every day. Nodes change as positions open and close. This is Friday's map. Monday's could look different. It backs up the levels, it doesn't replace them. Close above 685 and I'm redrawing everything.

And there's two headlines this week that can blow this whole setup up

1. The "Stand with Jensen" petition. 43K+ signatures, thousands of actual Nvidia employees, Musk signed it, big shareholders are literally writing the board telling them to keep his return on the table. Jensen comes back = NVDA squeeze = QQQ drop scenario probably gets delayed.

2. NVDA earnings Tuesday. Clean beat, good guidance, this gets delayed again. Simple as that.

So yeah. Trap confirmed Friday, path is 660 → 647 → 650 node → 620s. But I'm not marrying it. Two binary headlines this week can flip it in a day.

Twelve Knots, Twelve Surfaces That Turn Like Pages

Every knot is the edge of a surface. For the torus links T(p, q) there is an exact one: the Milnor fibre.

On the 3-sphere S^3 = {(z, w) : |z|^2 + |w|^2 = 1}, take the polynomial z^p + w^q. Its zero set is the torus link T(p, q), the thick tube in each panel. The points where its angle equals theta form a surface

F_theta = {(z, w) in S^3 : arg(z^p + w^q) = theta}

whose boundary is exactly the link: a Seifert surface.

As theta turns, the surface sweeps through all of S^3 while its edge stays still, like the pages of an open book bound along the knot. After one full turn every surface is back on itself (the monodromy). S^3 is drawn in 3D by stereographic projection, so once per turn a corner of each page runs out through infinity and comes back from the other side.

Panels: T(2,2), T(2,3), T(2,4), T(3,3), T(2,5), T(3,4), T(2,7), T(3,5), T(4,4), T(4,5), T(3,7), T(5,5). T(2,3) is the trefoil and T(2,2) is the Hopf link. The grid lines are arg z = const and arg w = const on each surface.

$SPY $QQQ WEEKLY MARKET RECAP & OUTLOOK 13 NOVEMBER

Friday’s close reinforced my bearish thesis. Despite several recovery attempts, I still expect another leg lower towards the $735 gap fill and potentially the 200 day SMA around $729.

1. SPY Failed breakout and bearish structure

The push towards $763 increasingly looks like a liquidity grab and failed breakout rather than a sustainable recovery.

SPY closed below its 5, 20, 50 and 100 day SMAs, alongside its 20 week SMA. Only the 10 day and 200 day SMAs remain below price.

The 10 day SMA remains below the 100 day, and Friday confirmed another bearish crossover: the 20 day SMA closed below the 100 day.

This suggests weakness is spreading into the intermediate trend.

Historically, these crossovers have frequently preceded tests of the 200 day SMA at least, although not every signal succeeds, the win rate is about 76%.

Key levels:

$749–751: Immediate support
$741–740: Next support
$735: Potential gap fill
$732.71: Recent swing low
$729: 200 day SMA

Resistance: $758–760, then the 50 day SMA around $764.

2. QQQ: Technology remains vulnerable

QQQ briefly reclaimed its 200 day SMA but failed to sustain it, closing around $679 below the 200 day SMA at $681.

It’s also below its 20 week SMA and other major daily averages. Hardly convincing evidence that the bottom is in.

3. VIX: Another volatility expansion?

After spiking to 28.36, VIX retraced towards $17.39 support before recovering to 19.30, potentially forming a higher low.

A sustained break above 20.37 would strengthen the bearish equity scenario. Losing 17.39 would weaken it.

4. Macro and next week’s catalysts

Persistent inflation, resilient employment and restrictive monetary conditions remain concerns. December Fed tightening expectations, a stronger dollar and rising yields could add pressure to risk assets.

Tuesday: Nvidia earnings: Oversold doesn’t automatically mean bullish. Guidance and expectations will determine the reaction.

Thursday: Anthropic’s anticipated IPO: A major offering could temporarily absorb market liquidity, although that’s not guaranteed.

My preferred scenario is further downside towards $735 and potentially $729.

If the decline doesn’t materialise before Nvidia’s earnings, the outlook becomes less straightforward. We could consolidate or rally towards resistance before another rejection.

I’m bearish on the structure, not predicting a guaranteed Black Monday. Monday could open green or flat without changing the broader bearish thesis.

5. What invalidates my thesis?

A sustained reclaim of SPY’s 50 day SMA around $764–765 would be the first serious warning.

A subsequent bullish 10/100 day SMA crossover would provide stronger confirmation of an intermediate trend reversal.

Until then, repeated resistance rejections, bearish crossovers, QQQ & SPY below their 20 weekly SMAs and a potentially recovering VIX suggest we’re not out of the woods yet.

6. Weekly trading recap: Winners AND losers

Tuesday’s bear trap caught me, costing a little over 30% on that options position.

A second short attempt near resistance also failed, triggering my -30% hard stop.

Then Friday’s bearish swing delivered approximately +120% on the options position, recovering those earlier losses and leaving me profitable for the week.

That’s why risk management matters. You don’t need to win every trade. You need to control losses and capitalise when the right setup arrives.

Bottom line: My bias remains bearish below the 50 day SMA. I’m watching for another leg lower towards $735 and the 200 day SMA, but I’ll adapt if price invalidates the setup.

Being a good trader isn’t about being permanently right. It’s about having a thesis, clear invalidation levels and the discipline to adjust.

Have a great weekend!✌️

$QQQ TRAP CONFIRMED: CLOSED BELOW 685. HERE IS THE FULL MAP

Where it is now:
•Closed 679.89 (-1.20%). Range today 671.71 to 688.75.
•Below every moving average that matters: 8 EMA 682, 200 EMA 685, 21 EMA 695, 50 EMA 708.
•RSI 42.8. Not oversold. Not washed out.
•Down 10.9% from the October 6 high of 762.86.
•Volume 41.3M, below the 50.6M average. This is controlled selling, not capitulation.

What just happened:
The bounce lived in the 685 to 711 trap zone for two days and got rejected at 695 three straight sessions. It never saw 700. Today it closed under 685, and PPI came in cooler than expected and the market sold off anyway. When good news cannot lift it, the path of least resistance is down.

Path 1, the trap plays out (base case):
660 is next, the early November pivot.
A close below 647, the November closing low, opens the January shelf at 620 to 630. That is the zone where this correction most likely ends.
VIX closed 19.30. Still no capitulation spike. Real bottoms in this cycle printed a VIX spike first, then a 30%+ crush. Neither has happened.

Path 2, the repair job:
A fast reclaim of 685 only puts it back inside the trap. That is not bullish, it is undecided.
Bulls need a close above 695, then 700, then the trap top at 711. That is three closes of work, not one green day.

Invalidation:
A daily close above 711 kills the bearish thesis completely.
A close back above 695 is the first warning that the trap is failing.

Until one of those prints, every bounce into 685 to 695 is a short opportunity, not a bottom.
